resale_co.name: Continued Certificate of Occupancy (housing inspection)
resale_co.issued_by: Office of Housing & Zoning (Zoning / Code Enforcement Officer)
requirements: Remove trash and debris inside and out; cut high grass and weeds; no standing water
Walkways, steps and driveways free of tripping hazards; accessory structures sound
Pools clean with self-closing, self-latching gates
No more than one unregistered vehicle
Sound siding, roof, flashing, gutters, foundation, chimney and structural members; exterior wood and metal protected and painted
House and unit numbers visible from the street
Handrails on stairs with more than 4 risers; guardrails at least 30 inches high
Windows open and stay open, with screens and unbroken glass; exterior doors open from inside without a key
Interior surfaces free of peeling paint; privacy locks on bedroom and bathroom doors; bathroom window or exhaust fan; dryer vented outside
Plumbing, water heater (110 degrees, discharge pipe about 6 inches from the floor) and heating system in safe working order
Carbon monoxide detector outside the bedroom areas
Two outlets per habitable room; GFCI outlets within 6 feet of water, in bathrooms, laundry and outdoors
Proof of extermination if insects or rodents are found; wood stoves inspected by a licensed chimney inspector
Work done without permits must be permitted and finaled
Passing County Health Department water test and septic certification (or waiver), and a passing fire inspection report from the Bridgeton Fire Department
resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Township's Application for Continued Certificate of Occupancy (owner, seller's agent, buyer's agent, owner's future address) and pay at the time of application by cash, check or money order payable to Greenwich Township. The Township building is not regularly staffed; mail to Greenwich Township, P.O. Box 64, Greenwich, NJ 08323, or contact the Zoning / Code Enforcement Officer. The fee amounts are blank on the posted form.

resale_co.notes: Greenwich posts an Application for Continued Certificate of Occupancy (asks for the seller's agent, the buyer's agent and the owner's future address, so it is used for sales) and a December 2025 list of common housing inspection violations that requires County water and septic certifications and a Bridgeton fire inspection report. No Township page states in words that a CCO is required on every sale, and no fee is published: the form's fee lines are blank and the 'Fee Schedule 2023' section on the Planning Documents page is empty. The Township Code is on ecode360 (GR4098) and could not be opened. The form uses the same wording as Commercial Township's CCO form. Construction permits are handled by Teresa Warburton (856-455-9591, twarburton@upperdeerfield.com) at the Upper Deerfield Construction Office.

requirements: Smoke alarms (UL listed) on every level; battery-only alarms must be the 10-year sealed battery type, and hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms
Basement smoke alarm at the bottom of the stairwell, on the ceiling (not between joists)
A 10-year sealed smoke alarm in every bedroom
Smoke alarms and CO alarms must be less than 10 years old and working
Carbon monoxide alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms
House numbers at least 4 inches high, contrasting color, permanently fixed and visible from the street
Homes with solar panels, a backup generator or battery storage need a permanent printed 'Caution: Multiple Sources of Power' label at the main electrical panel and the electric meter
If there is a fire alarm system, a report from the alarm company is required (per the online application form)

authorities.name: City of Bridgeton Fire Department, Bureau of Fire Prevention
authorities.area_served: Entire township (City of Bridgeton Fire Department under a shared service)
authorities.lead_time: Submit the request 2 to 3 weeks before settlement; the lowest fee applies when the request is received 10 or more business days before settlement.

fees.label: Smoke/CO certificate, 1-2 family, request received 10 or more business days before settlement
fees.quote: Requests received 10 business days or more prior to settlement date or change of occupant $45.00

fees.quote: Requests received 7 business days prior to settlement date or change of occupant $90.00

fees.label: Smoke/CO certificate, 1-2 family, request received fewer than 4 business days before settlement
fees.quote: Requests received fewer than 4 business days prior to settlement date or change of occupant $161.00

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the online 'CO and Smoke Certification Application' (Google Form) linked from the Bridgeton Fire Department's Uniform Fire Code page, picking Greenwich Township as the municipality. Payment is due at the time of the inspection by check or money order payable to the City of Bridgeton Fire Department (the form says an online payment link will be on the invoice). Re-inspection for a failed or no-show inspection costs the same as the first inspection. The certificate is emailed to the address given and is valid for 90 days. Questions: firedepartment@cityofbridgeton.com or 856-451-0090 / 856-451-0091.

fire_cert.notes: The Township's Planning Documents page says the City of Bridgeton Fire Department's Fire Marshal's Office does the smoke/CO certification inspections for Greenwich, and the Bridgeton online application lists Greenwich Township. The Township directory names Brittany Snyder of the Bridgeton Fire Marshal's Office as Greenwich's Fire Marshal; she is listed in the Bridgeton Bureau of Fire Prevention with the email snyderb@cityofbridgeton.com (linked from her name on the Bridgeton Department page). Jack Justice Jr. is the appointed Fire Official. Fees, lead time and 90-day validity come from the Bridgeton Bureau's guideline sheet (created November 20, 2025).
